features: Fixed: the instalment plan page did not see the credit of someone who had paid more than owed. The engine recognises credit in two forms — a negative opening balance and an overpayment (someone who paid more than their instalment) — but the instalment plan page only showed one. For an owner who had overpaid, the "Credits (Advances)" card did not count it, the "Collected" card declared less money than had actually come in, and their row carried no "Credit" badge. The defect dates back to beta.9, which introduced the second form of credit without updating this page.

Verified on real data, on a plan generated by the real engine (not on test fixtures): an owner owed € 500.00 and paid € 700.00. Before the fix the page declared € 500.00 collected and no credit; it now correctly declares € 1,200.00 collected (summed with the other owners) and € 200.00 in credit.

The instalment plan page now has a detailed in-app guide, opened from the "Guide" button at the top: what every button in the action bar does, what each instalment colour means — including the two forms of credit — how issuing works, and what actually happens when removing an item or recalculating the plan. It was entirely missing until now: the only explanation was the three summary cards at the top of the page.

Fixed: on a phone screen, the button bar above the instalments table scrolled horizontally with no visual hint — the last button, "Move expense", was only reachable by someone who happened to swipe. A fade on the right edge now signals there is more to see.

Fixed a small defect found while writing the guide: the "Updating..." indicator on the "Budget coverage" section read the wrong flag by mistake and never appeared while loading. Also removed a "credits only" filter that existed in the code with no button anywhere to turn it on, and an unused icon import.

Fixed: the "Move expense" feature moved budget from one item to another to cover an unexpected cost, but offered no way back — the message that blocked removing an involved item had always promised you could "reverse the movements", an action that did not actually exist. The item that had given up funds stayed blocked forever, even for movements from other instalment plans, and it was possible to move away budget that matched expenses already recorded. The explanatory text also promised an automatic year-end recovery that was never built.

Added a real "Reverse" button in each item's history: it creates an opposite movement that returns the funds, without deleting or changing the original. The block on removal now checks the item's actual balance within the current plan, no longer just whether a past movement exists anywhere or on another plan, and it is no longer possible to move away budget matching invoices already recorded. An item that gave up funds and remains uncovered is now flagged with a "From Move expense" label, both on the current plan and in the item picker of a new instalment plan, so it is clear why coverage is missing. The feature's explanatory text now says how things really work: recovery is not automatic and requires a following instalment plan.

Fully verified on screen on a real condominium: created a budget movement, reversed it successfully, and created a new instalment plan by selecting the very item left uncovered — generated correctly, with the amount and the split among owners matching to the cent.

Fixed: in the "Instalment Schedule" PDF, an owner with a credit on a single instalment saw that cell shown empty (a dash), but the column total at the bottom of the table still summed it in. Adding up the visible cells by eye gave a different number from the printed total: the total was always correct, the cell was hiding the figure that made it up.
This update changes the database structure: a migration adds a column to the budget movements table, to record reversals.
